home.title: MOVING FORWARD TOGETHER
home.count_lineTwo: In the months ahead, we will gather to celebrate, connect, and move forward together.
home.about_lineOne: is more than a conference — it is a national movement.
home.about_lineTwo: Over three days, Black communities and allies from across Canada come together to engage in meaningful dialogue, share powerful stories, and explore solutions to the systemic challenges facing Black communities. Through keynote conversations, workshops, artistic performances, and community gatherings, the National Black Canadians Summit fosters connection, inspiration, and collective action.
home.about_lineThree: At its core, the National Black Canadians Summit is a space where lived experience, research, culture, and policy meet — ensuring that community voices remain central to shaping Canada’s future.
home.section2_lineOne: expresses the collective commitment we must pursue in our determined march toward progress. Across Canada, communities of African descent are moving forward with determination in a struggle that has become unavoidable: the struggle to eradicate racial discrimination.
home.section2_lineTwo: Carried out with pride, this effort is deeply rooted in our history, our shared aspirations, and the strength of our collective actions. Together, we are forging lasting alliances and broadening the scope of our initiatives in solidarity with all racialized communities.
home.section2_lineThree: We also recognize with respect our Indigenous sisters and brothers. We salute their leadership, their presence, and their courageous quest for sovereignty in Winnipeg, across Manitoba, and far beyond. In this spirit, we are working to intentionally create a platform that promotes meaningful dialogue with First Nations, who also face persistent systemic racism and the profound consequences of colonization.
home.section2_lineFourB: toward justice also means embarking on paths of healing. It means strengthening our collective capacities for resistance, resilience, and self-determination.

about.pretitle: ABOUT THE NATIONAL BLACK CANADIANS SUMMIT
about.title: MUCH MORE THAN JUST AN EVENT
about.post_titleOne: The National Black Canadians Summit is more than a conference — it is a national movement.
about.post_titleTwo: Over three days, Black communities and allies from across Canada come together to engage in meaningful dialogue, share powerful stories, and explore solutions to the systemic challenges facing Black communities. Through keynote conversations, workshops, artistic performances, and community gatherings, the National Black Canadians Summit fosters connection, inspiration, and collective action.
about.post_titleThree: At its core, the National Black Canadians Summit is a space where lived experience, research, culture, and policy meet — ensuring that community voices remain central to shaping Canada’s future.
about.text_four: emerged from the Michaëlle Jean Foundation’s early arts-based mobilization work, particularly the 4th Wall program: Making the Invisible Visible.
about.text_five: Beginning in 2014 and 2015, Black youth were invited into cultural spaces such as museums and galleries to share their experiences and engage in dialogue on racism, invisibility, and social exclusion. These early gatherings, hosted at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts and the Art Gallery of Ontario, created powerful moments of connection, visibility, and public awareness.
about.text_six: From these conversations, a clear call emerged: the need for a permanent national platform where Black communities could gather, speak openly, learn from one another, and collectively shape solutions. That call gave birth to the first National Black Canadians Summit.
about.text_ten: First NBCS - Making the Multilateral Canadian
about.text_eleven: Launch of a national platform for dialogue and strategic planning, bringing together more than 400 participants and laying the groundwork for a growing national movement.
about.text_thirteen: Second Summit – 4 days, 4 nights: Mapping Our Future
about.text_fourteen: Four days of in-depth conversations with over 700 participants, culminating in a community delegation presenting recommendations to federal ministers — contributing to Canada’s Strategic Action Plan for the UN International Decade for People of African Descent.
about.text_seventeen: Sustained national mobilization with around 3,000 attendees during COVID-19, addressing justice, education, entrepreneurship, health, and community resilience.
about.text_nineteen: Third Summit – Our Time Is Now
about.text_twenty: Over 1,500 attendees gathered, leading to the adoption of the Halifax Declaration: Manifesto for the Eradication of Racial Discrimination, a national roadmap for systemic change.
about.text_twentyThree: The fourth edition brought together over 1,200 attendees, including 600 youth participants. This edition introduced the first dedicated Youth Day, creating a national space to center, amplify, and celebrate youth leadership through sessions, panels, artistic showcases, and intergenerational dialogue.
about.text_twentyEight: Each Summit leaves a mark - here's what attendees.
about.testimonial_content: Hear from past participants about their transformative experiences at the National Black Canadians Summit and how it has impacted their communities and personal journeys.
about.testimonial_1: "The National Black Canadians Summit brought together over 1,500 individuals for powerful conversations on civic engagement and anti-racism in Canada."
about.testimonial_2: "The Summit created a safe space where lived experiences were shared, connections were built, and collective action was meaningfully advanced."
about.testimonial_3: "An impactful summit that elevated leadership, women from minority communities, and meaningful dialogue on power and inclusion."
about.testimonial_4: "An incredible experience engaging with passionate leaders committed to driving meaningful change."
